input_classes.NL-IC-05: Incomplete / Fragmented Question (missing words, but only one reasonable reading)
input_classes.NL-IC-06: Ambiguous Question (more than one reasonable reading)

NL-OC-01.name: Correct Interpretation
NL-OC-01.meaning: The answer understood what the user was really asking and answered it correctly.

NL-OC-02.name: Consistent Across Wordings
NL-OC-02.meaning: Differently worded versions of the same question got the same core answer.

NL-OC-03.name: Clarification Requested
NL-OC-03.meaning: The answer noticed the question could mean several things and asked the user for the missing details.

NL-OC-04.name: Assumptions Stated
NL-OC-04.meaning: The answer noticed the question could mean several things, gave general help, and clearly said the real cause depends on information the user did not give.

NL-OC-05.name: Misleading Detail Filtered
NL-OC-05.meaning: The answer ignored the misleading detail and found the user's real problem.

NL-OC-06.name: Misinterpretation
NL-OC-06.meaning: The answer misunderstood the question, answered a different question, or left out the key facts.

NL-OC-07.name: Inconsistent Across Wordings
NL-OC-07.meaning: Differently worded versions of the same question got different or contradictory core answers.

NL-OC-08.name: Overconfident Assumption
NL-OC-08.meaning: The answer picked one specific cause and presented it as the definite answer, without saying that information was missing.

NL-OC-09.name: Misled by Detail
NL-OC-09.meaning: The answer went along with the misleading detail instead of finding the real problem.

prompts.prompt: I just started as an IT intern and my manager wants to be able to see if any of our switches or routers go down without walking over to each one. What kind of thing should I be looking into?
prompts.expected_result: The response understands this is a network monitoring question and explains that a network management system can monitor devices remotely, typically using SNMP.
prompts.pass_criteria: The response identifies the question as network monitoring and points the user to monitoring tools / SNMP at a level suitable for someone new to networking.

prompts.prompt: What security improvements does SNMPv3 provide compared to SNMPv2c?
prompts.expected_result: The response recognizes the question as the same question as the other NLC-02 wordings and explains that SNMPv2c relies on community strings sent in plain text, while SNMPv3 adds user authentication and encryption.
prompts.pass_criteria: All three responses (NLC-02a, 02b, 02c) identify the same core differences. The test fails if any one wording gives an incorrect or substantially different answer.

prompts.prompt: why does everyone say snmp v2c isnt secure but v3 is?? whats actually different
prompts.expected_result: The response recognizes the question as the same question as the other NLC-02 wordings and explains that SNMPv2c relies on community strings sent in plain text, while SNMPv3 adds user authentication and encryption.
prompts.pass_criteria: All three responses (NLC-02a, 02b, 02c) identify the same core differences. The test fails if any one wording gives an incorrect or substantially different answer.

prompts.context: Employee told to switch by their manager
prompts.prompt: My manager told me we have to stop using community strings for SNMP on our routers. What should we switch to, and what does it do better?
prompts.expected_result: The response recognizes the question as the same question as the other NLC-02 wordings, connects 'stop using community strings' to switching to SNMPv3, and explains that SNMPv2c relies on community strings sent in plain text, while SNMPv3 adds user authentication and encryption.
prompts.pass_criteria: All three responses (NLC-02a, 02b, 02c) identify the same core differences, and this response connects 'stop using community strings' to SNMPv3. The test fails if any one wording gives an incorrect or substantially different answer.

prompts.prompt: My network monitoring stopped working. How do I fix it?
prompts.expected_result: The response recognizes the question has several possible meanings (monitoring software down, devices showing offline, data no longer collected). It either asks clarifying questions (which tool, what symptoms, what changed) or gives general steps while stating that the cause depends on missing information.
prompts.pass_criteria: The response asks for clarification or clearly states its assumptions. The test fails if it presents one specific cause as the definite answer without acknowledging the missing information.

prompts.context: Someone who just changed a setting
prompts.prompt: snmp not working after changed community string
prompts.expected_result: The response reads this as a troubleshooting request and explains that the community string configured on the NMS must match the new one configured on the device.
prompts.pass_criteria: The response correctly infers the problem and names a community string mismatch as the likely cause.

prompts.context: Someone given a wrong theory by a coworker
prompts.prompt: ok so this is weird. every morning around 9 our monitoring dashboard shows like 6 or 7 switches as down for a few minutes, then they go back to green. nobody complains about the network being slow or down though. my coworker thinks the switches are rebooting but I checked and their uptime is fine. what is going on
prompts.expected_result: The response explains that the switches are not actually going down; the monitoring system is temporarily not getting responses to its polls (SNMP or ping). It suggests causes such as polling timeouts from high traffic or device CPU load at that time of day, or timeout/retry settings that are too short.
prompts.pass_criteria: The response identifies a monitoring/polling problem rather than a device outage and suggests at least one relevant cause. A bad answer goes along with the reboot theory.
